Product Name

Nexora
Tagline: Connect. Collab. Craft.

Product Description (Core Context)

Design a community-based social collaboration platform called Nexora, built specifically for students and freshers to collaborate on projects, network professionally, and engage in domain-focused discussions — all in a single unified platform.

Currently, students are forced to use:

LinkedIn → networking & professional presence

GitHub → code & project collaboration

Discord → discussions & communities

These platforms are fragmented and not project-centric.

Nexora solves this by acting as a hybrid of LinkedIn + GitHub + Discord, with a project-first approach, enabling career growth through real collaboration rather than passive connections.

Core Philosophy

Communities come first

Projects drive networking

Profiles evolve through contributions

Collaboration > scrolling

Target Audience

Engineering & CS students

Fresh graduates

Hackathon participants

Open-source beginners

College project teams

UI & UX Reference

Primary UI inspiration: Discord

Additional inspiration: GitHub Projects, LinkedIn profiles

Key difference: Every space supports projects, not just chat

Visual Style

Theme: Modern, tech-focused, community-driven

Look & Feel: Discord-like layout with cleaner, more professional polish

Color Palette:

Primary: Indigo / Blue

Accent: Cyan / Teal

Background: Light Gray & Dark Mode (Discord-style)

Typography: Inter / Poppins

Components: Rounded cards, subtle shadows, minimal gradients

Icons: Clean line icons

App Structure & Screens
1️⃣ Landing Screen

Nexora logo + tagline

Headline:
“Where students connect, collaborate, and craft real projects.”

CTA:

Get Started

Explore Communities

Abstract visuals representing people, nodes, and projects

2️⃣ Authentication

Email / Google sign-in

Clean, minimal forms

Student-friendly onboarding

3️⃣ Main App Layout (Discord-Like)

Split layout:

Left Sidebar: Communities (Servers)

Middle Panel: Channels / Projects / Discussions

Right Panel: Active members / Project contributors

4️⃣ Communities (Domain-Based Servers)

Each community represents a domain or interest.

Examples:

Web Development

AI / ML

DSA & Competitive Programming

Cybersecurity

Mobile App Development

Community layout:

Description & stats

Channels:

#announcements

#general-discussion

#project-ideas

#ongoing-projects

#completed-projects

5️⃣ Community Dashboard

Each community dashboard displays:

Active projects

Proposed projects

Completed projects

Project history timeline

Popular contributors

Users can join multiple communities and browse their project histories before joining.

6️⃣ Project Spaces (Key Feature)

Every project has a dedicated space, similar to a Discord channel but project-focused.

Each project space includes:

Project overview

Tech stack tags

Contributors list

Task board (To Do / In Progress / Done)

Discussion thread

File & link sharing

Project status:

Proposed

Ongoing

Completed

7️⃣ Create Project Flow

Button: “Start a Project”

Steps:

Project name & description

Select community

Required skills

Team size

Visibility (public / community-only)

Clean stepper UI

8️⃣ User Profiles (LinkedIn + GitHub Hybrid)

Profile includes:

Name, role, college

Bio

Skills

GitHub & LinkedIn links

Resume / CV section

Project contributions

Communities joined

Reputation / contribution score

Profiles grow based on actual project work, not just connections.

9️⃣ Activity Feed

Shows:

New project proposals

Projects completed

Members joining teams

Community announcements

Minimal feed — no unnecessary social noise.

🔟 Messaging & Notifications

1:1 chats

Project group chats

Mentions & invites

Task assignment alerts

Navigation

Discord-style sidebar navigation

Keyboard-friendly

Mobile responsive with bottom navigation

UX Priorities

Discover projects quickly

Reduce friction in collaboration

Encourage contribution over passive scrolling

Clear separation of discussion vs execution

Deliverables Required

High-fidelity UI mockups

Mobile + Web views

Dark mode variant

Clickable prototype

Reusable component system

Design Emphasis

Professional yet student-friendly

Scalable for future features

Feels like a real startup product, not a college demo

**Defining Nexora's Scope**

I'm solidifying the core concept: a high-fidelity React app for Nexora. It's envisioned as a student-focused platform, blending elements of LinkedIn, GitHub, and Discord. The focus is on three key pillars: community, project management, and professional profiles, all in a modern UI.


**Refining UI Details**

I'm now focusing on the aesthetic and technical specifics of the UI, aiming for a tech-focused design with a preference for dark mode and an indigo/blue color palette. I've initiated project setup with `metadata.json`, `index.tsx`, etc., and plan to use React Context or a basic state management strategy. My component breakdown includes Sidebar, ChannelList, ProjectBoard, ProfileView, LandingPage, and Feed, all to be styled with Tailwind CSS for a professional yet Discord-esque feel. The app's core structure includes a clear component breakdown.

🔁 FOLLOW-UP UI REFINEMENT PROMPT — NEXORA

Apply the following design corrections and refinements to the existing Nexora UI prototype. Do not redesign from scratch.

1️⃣ Brand Identity Clarification

Ensure Nexora has its own distinct visual identity.

Avoid layouts, spacing, iconography, or color usage that feels like a direct clone of Discord.

Maintain a modern SaaS-style interface, not a chat-app clone.

Use white as the primary background, with blue/green accents.

Add an optional dark mode toggle in settings (dark gray base with blue/green highlights).

2️⃣ Communities Model Update

Communities must be user-created and interest-based, not fixed or domain-restricted.

Remove any hard-coded categories like AI/ML, Cloud, Web Dev.

Communities should instead be discoverable via:

Tags

Keywords

Popularity

Activity level

3️⃣ Landing Page Adjustment

Keep the landing page simple and introductory.

Focus on explaining:

What Nexora is

Who it is for

Why it exists

Include a single primary CTA: Get Started

Clicking Get Started should trigger Login / Sign Up.

4️⃣ Main App Layout Behavior

Left sidebar should show:

A top “+” button for Explore Communities / Create Community

Below it, a list of communities the user has joined

This sidebar behavior should remain consistent across the app.

5️⃣ New User / No Community State

If a user is not part of any community:

Show a default home screen prompting:

Explore Communities

Create a Community

This should also be the default view immediately after login, until a community is selected.

6️⃣ Explore Communities Flow

In the Explore Communities section:

Display community cards

Allow users to:

View community dashboard

Join community

Browsing communities should not require joining first.

7️⃣ Community Internal Structure Refinement

Each community should include:

General communication channels

Roles & permissions

Add a distinct “Project Spaces” section inside each community’s sidebar.

8️⃣ Project Spaces Logic

Project Spaces are a subsection of a community, created by default.

Users can:

Browse all projects in the community

View project descriptions and requirements

Only users who are part of a project can:

Chat inside that project space

Access project-specific discussions

Non-members can view details but cannot interact.

9️⃣ Project Channel Behavior

Project channels should:

Display project overview at the top

Show required roles/skills

Indicate project status (Proposed / Ongoing / Completed)

Chat and collaboration tools should be restricted to project members only.

🔟 UX Consistency

Maintain clean routing and clear separation between:

Communities

Community chats

Project spaces

Ensure navigation feels intuitive and not overwhelming.

Prioritize clarity over density.

✅ Expected Outcome

**Refining Nexora's Identity**

Okay, I'm focusing on Nexora's visual identity now. It's crucial this feels distinct, not derivative. White background as the core, with blue and green accents seems the way to go. I'm prioritizing user-created content and interests as the foundation, and removing those static categories in favor of customizable options. I'm also planning to add a dark mode toggle for users.


**Developing the Application Structure**

I'm now diving into the application architecture. I'm focusing on user onboarding with a simple introduction, "Get Started" to Login/Sign Up. The sidebar is consistent, with "+" for exploration and creation, and a list of joined communities. The home screen defaults to community exploration or creation. Displaying community cards without requiring join-in for browsing is a priority. I'm also planning general channels, roles, and permissions, and dedicated "Project Spaces".
